Socket’s Threat Research Team is tracking an active supply chain compromise affecting widely used keyv and cacheable npm packages. On August 4, 2026, at least ten packages in those namespaces and additional packages owned by other maintainers were published with a malicious preinstall hook. The affected packages collectively account for tens of millions of weekly downloads, and Socket says new packages are appearing in real time.

The evidence indicates the maintainer account Jaredwray was compromised and used to publish across the keyv and cacheable package families. The malicious setup.mjs loader downloads a standalone Bun runtime and uses it to execute an obfuscated second-stage payload called Math_Symbol.js. That payload harvests cloud and CI credentials, npm tokens, GitHub-related secrets, Vault tokens, Kubernetes service account tokens, and other secrets found on disk.

The payload can also propagate by using stolen npm tokens to discover packages, inject the same hook and payload files, bump versions, and republish trojanized releases through npm OIDC trusted publishing. Stolen data is committed to threat actor GitHub repositories and delivered to DNS-resolved destinations, while persistence is planted through .claude, .vscode, and a host-level GitHub token monitor. Socket recommends treating any environment that installed an affected version and ran install scripts as compromised, removing the dead-man’s switch and implant artifacts before rotating reachable credentials.

  • The malicious package code was byte-identical to a clean release candidate except for package.json and two added lifecycle files, so file comparisons of the normal library output alone would not reveal the compromise.
  • The article warns that rotating or revoking stolen GitHub tokens before removing the installed monitor can trigger its dead-man’s switch, which evaluates a remote-supplied command when the token starts returning HTTP 4xx responses.
  • The compromised keyv release had valid provenance because the legitimate release workflow built already-trojanized source, showing that provenance can confirm how software was built without proving the source was safe.
  • The loader downloads and runs a standalone Bun runtime from GitHub, which may bypass defenses focused only on Node processes even though the compromise starts through an npm preinstall script.
  • The source repository persistence in .claude and .vscode can execute the same loader when a developer or AI coding agent opens the cloned repository, meaning infection does not require running npm install in that scenario.

Attackers took over a maintainer account and published poisoned versions of popular npm packages in the keyv and cacheable families, plus some others, so the harmful code could run automatically when those packages were installed. People and companies using software that depends on these packages may be affected even if they never chose them directly, because they sit deep inside common software dependency chains. The code can steal cloud, GitHub, npm, and other work credentials, then use them to publish more poisoned packages, which could spread the problem across many projects with tens of millions of weekly downloads.

This is a must-read because it reports an active supply chain compromise affecting widely used npm packages with tens of millions of weekly downloads. The payload steals cloud, CI, GitHub, npm, Vault, and Kubernetes credentials, includes persistence, and can republish trojanized packages to spread further.

Calendar phishing, or “calphishing,” is emerging as a dangerous evolution of phishing that abuses employees’ calendar invites to steal credentials, bypass MFA, or trick victims into calling attackers. The risk is especially serious for busy healthcare workers who may not have time to scrutinize every calendar event.
KEY POINTS
  • 01Phishing remains the most common and damaging cyber threat, with 3.4 billion phishing emails sent daily.
  • 02Calendar phishing, or calphishing, delivers malicious content directly into an employee’s calendar.
  • 03Calphishing aims to trick victims into visiting fake login pages, approving authentication requests, or phoning hackers directly.
  • 04The goals of calphishing include capturing login credentials, obtaining authenticated access, stealing money, and in some campaigns targeting session tokens to bypass multifactor authentication.
  • 05The article says calphishing could be catastrophic for overburdened healthcare employees who do not have time to vet every calendar event.

The article is an op-ed by Errol Weiss, Chief Security Officer at Health ISAC, about calendar phishing, or calphishing. It says phishing remains the most common and damaging cyber threat, with 3.4 billion phishing emails sent daily. The article explains that phishing methods are evolving to take advantage of people’s busy work lives through their calendars.

Calphishing involves delivering malicious content directly into an employee’s calendar. The goal is to trick victims into visiting fake login pages, approving authentication requests, or phoning hackers directly and falling for a social engineering scam. As with other phishing, the end goal can be to capture login credentials, obtain authenticated access, or steal money directly from the victim.

The article notes that some clever calphishing campaigns also target session tokens, which maintain a user’s logged-in state. By targeting these tokens, attackers can bypass multifactor authentication and access internal systems without triggering additional verification protocols. The article warns that this could be catastrophic for overburdened healthcare employees who do not have time to vet every calendar event.

  • Calphishing shifts phishing from the inbox into calendar workflows, taking advantage of the fact that busy employees may treat calendar events as routine work items rather than suspicious messages.
  • Some calphishing campaigns target session tokens, which means attackers may be able to keep a user’s logged-in access without triggering additional multifactor authentication checks.
  • The article highlights phone calls as part of calphishing, showing that a calendar invite can be used to move victims into direct social engineering rather than only fake web pages.
  • Healthcare is presented as especially exposed because overburdened employees may not have time to vet every calendar event before acting on it.

The article explains that criminals are now using employees’ work calendars, not just email, to trick people into opening fake sign-in pages, approving access requests, or calling the criminals directly. This affects busy workers, especially in healthcare, who may not have time to carefully check every calendar invite. The stakes are high because these tricks can let criminals steal passwords, get into internal systems, or take money from victims.

AI red teaming is testing an AI system by trying to make it fail, leak data, or behave unsafely.
AI security concept
AI security is the practice of protecting artificial intelligence systems and their data from misuse, attacks, and unintended harm.
AI systems concept
AI systems are software or machines that use artificial intelligence to perform tasks such as analysis, prediction, or decision support.
AI tools tool
AI tools are software programs that use artificial intelligence to help with tasks such as writing, analysis, coding, or decision support.
AI usage concept
AI usage means how people or organizations use artificial intelligence tools, models, or systems.
AI workflows concept
AI workflows are step-by-step processes that use artificial intelligence tools to complete tasks or support decisions.
AI-native concept
AI-native describes a product or system designed around artificial intelligence from the start rather than adding AI features later.
AI-SPM concept
AI Security Posture Management, a category of tools that monitor and enforce security policies for artificial intelligence systems and models.
Aikido product

Aliases are alternate names used for the same person, group, malware, domain, or tool.
Allegedly stolen data concept
Allegedly stolen data is information claimed to have been taken without permission but not necessarily independently confirmed.
allow-list concept
An allow-list is a list of approved senders or systems that are treated as trusted.
allowlist concept
An allowlist is a list of approved users, programs, websites, or actions that are permitted while others are blocked.
AltraVita organization

amazon-web-services product
Amazon Web Services is Amazon’s cloud computing platform that lets people rent servers, storage, and other online infrastructure.
AMD organization
AMD is a major semiconductor company that makes computer processors and graphics chips.
Americas Hobby Exercise other
Americas Hobby Exercise is a named exercise or event referenced in security reporting.

AMSI is a Microsoft Windows security interface that lets antivirus tools inspect scripts and other content before it runs.
analysts other
Analysts are people who examine data, alerts, or evidence to understand problems and make decisions.
Android product
Android is Google's mobile operating system used on many phones, tablets, and other devices.
Android TVs product

Anonymous usage metrics concept
Anonymous usage metrics are statistics about how people use a product that are collected without directly identifying individual users.
anthropic
Anthropic is an AI company known for the Claude family of AI assistants.

Anti-analysis checks are tricks malware uses to detect researchers' tools or sandboxes and hide its real behavior.
also: environment and anti-analysis checks, environment checks
Anti-analysis protections technique
Anti-analysis protections are tricks malware uses to make it harder for researchers or security tools to study it.
API protocol
An API is a way for one program to ask another program or service for data or actions.
API keys concept
API keys are secret codes used to let software access an online service.
API Token scopes concept
API Token scopes are permission limits that define what an API token is allowed to read, change, or delete.
API tokens concept
API tokens are digital keys used to let software access an application or service.

also: flexible APIs, Silent Push APIs, Data API access
APITokens concept

also: API Token
APK other

APK file concept

Apollo tool
Apollo is a named tool, framework, product, or component referenced in security reporting.
App Store product
Apple's digital marketplace for downloading and installing applications on iOS and macOS devices.
apple
Apple is a technology company that makes iPhones, Macs, iPads, and related software and services.
AppleScript tool
AppleScript is a macOS scripting language used to automate applications and system tasks.
Apple’s servers organization
Apple’s servers are computer systems operated by Apple to provide services such as iCloud, app delivery, and account features.
apps product
Apps are software programs that run on phones, computers, or web platforms to perform tasks for users.

Arbitrary code execution means an attacker can make a system run commands or programs of the attacker's choosing.

An artifact is a file, log entry, build output, or other item produced or found during software development or investigation.
Artifactory product
Artifactory is JFrog's software repository manager used to store and distribute build artifacts and packages.
artificial intelligence concept
Artificial intelligence is technology that lets computers perform tasks that usually need human-like thinking or pattern recognition.
attachment concept

attachments concept
Attachments are files sent along with emails or messages.
attack chains concept
Attack chains are sequences of steps an attacker follows to break in, move around, and achieve a goal.
attack path concept
An attack path is the chain of steps an attacker could take to reach a valuable target.
attack paths concept

attack surface management concept

attacker threat-actor

Attacker claims are statements made by criminals or hackers about what they did, which may or may not be true.
attacker sophistication concept
Attacker sophistication describes how skilled, well-resourced, and advanced an attacker’s methods are.
Attacker-controlled infrastructure concept
Attacker-controlled infrastructure means servers, domains, or online services that criminals operate to run attacks or receive stolen data.
attackers concept
Attackers are people or groups who try to break into systems, steal data, or cause harm online.
audit concept

audited concept
Audited means examined by reviewers to check whether something is accurate, secure, or compliant.
Auditing concept
Auditing is the process of reviewing records, settings, or activity to check whether rules are being followed.
australia
Australia is a country often referenced in cybersecurity reporting as a target, regulator, or law-enforcement partner.
authenticated concept
Authenticated means a person, device, or program has proven its identity to a system.
Authenticated access concept
Authenticated access means a user or system has proved its identity before being allowed to use a service or data.
Authenticated user concept
An authenticated user is someone who has successfully logged in or otherwise proven their identity to a system.
authentication concept
Authentication is the process of proving that a person or system is allowed to log in.
authentication bypass vulnerability
Authentication bypass is a flaw or technique that lets someone access a system without properly logging in.
authentication bypass flaw vulnerability
An authentication bypass flaw lets someone access a system without properly logging in.
authentication checks concept
Authentication checks are steps a system uses to confirm that a person or app is really who it claims to be.

Authentication requests are login or identity-check attempts sent to a system to prove who a user or device is.
authentication tokens concept
Authentication tokens are digital proof that a user or program has already signed in or been authorized.
authorities organization
Authorities are government or regulatory bodies that may investigate incidents, enforce laws, or issue guidance.
Authorization concept
Authorization is the process of deciding what a logged-in user or system is allowed to access or do.
automated attack technique

Automated security workflows technique
Automated security workflows are preset steps that security tools run automatically, such as collecting evidence, opening tickets, or blocking a suspicious address.
automated tools tool
Automated tools are software programs that perform tasks with little or no manual effort.
Automated workflows concept
Sequences of tasks executed automatically by software, which if compromised can be used to propagate malicious actions.
Automation concept
Automation uses software to perform tasks with little or no human intervention.
autonomous AI concept
Autonomous AI is artificial intelligence that can make decisions or take actions with limited human direction.
Autonomous-system check technique
An autonomous-system check is a way to identify or filter network traffic based on the internet routing network it comes from.

AWS Security Hub Extended plan is a named plan or package associated with AWS Security Hub coverage or purchasing in security reporting.

aws-security-hub-extended product

Azure product

Azure DevOps product
Azure DevOps is Microsoft's cloud service for managing software development, source code, builds, testing, and deployments.
azure-websites product
azure-websites is a name commonly associated with Microsoft Azure App Service website hosting domains or resources.

backend infrastructure concept
The behind-the-scenes servers, databases, and networking that power a website or application.
backups concept

Bandwidth is the amount of data a network connection can carry in a given time.

berapt-medii[.]com other

binary concept
A file containing machine-readable code that a computer can run directly, as opposed to human-readable source code.
bitdefender organization

black-hat-usa

blockchain concept

brazil other

breach concept

Breach at the Beach is a cybersecurity event or training name referenced in security reporting.
breached concept
Breached means a system, account, or data was accessed or exposed without authorization.
Breaches concept
Breaches are security incidents where attackers gain unauthorized access to systems, accounts, or data.
BreachLock organization
BreachLock is a cybersecurity company that provides penetration testing and attack-simulation services.
break-ins concept

breaking changes concept

cambodia other

canada

claude

cloud concept

code execution technique

codex

also: ScreenConnect agent, ScreenConnect client

containers concept

cookie concept

cookies concept

A fixed-size string generated by a mathematical algorithm from input data, used to verify integrity or store passwords.
HashiCorp Vault product
HashiCorp Vault is a tool for securely storing and controlling access to secrets such as passwords, API keys, and certificates.
HashiCorp Vault tokens concept
HashiCorp Vault tokens are credentials used to authenticate to HashiCorp Vault and access stored secrets.
header From domain protocol
The header From domain is the domain shown in the visible sender address of an email.
Health Care and Social Assistance Threat Landscape Report other
A Health Care and Social Assistance Threat Landscape Report is a report describing cyber threats affecting healthcare and social assistance organizations.
Health Sector concept
The part of the economy consisting of healthcare providers, insurers, and related organizations.
Health Sector Heartbeat other
Health Sector Heartbeat is a security-related report, publication, or program focused on healthcare sector cyber issues.
health-isac
Health-ISAC is an information-sharing group that helps healthcare organizations exchange cyber threat intelligence.
Health-ISAC Community Champion other
Health-ISAC Community Champion is a recognition or role associated with the Health-ISAC cybersecurity community.
Health-ISAC Health Sector Heartbeat Q2 Report organization
Health-ISAC Health Sector Heartbeat Q2 Report is a Health-ISAC report summarizing cybersecurity trends and issues in the health sector for a quarter.
Health-ISAC members organization
Health-ISAC members are organizations that belong to the Health Information Sharing and Analysis Center to share healthcare cybersecurity threat information.
Health-ISAC’s Inaugural CISO Benchmarking Report organization
Health-ISAC’s Inaugural CISO Benchmarking Report is a Health-ISAC publication comparing security leadership practices across healthcare organizations.
Healthcare and medical technology organizations organization
Healthcare and medical technology organizations are hospitals, clinics, suppliers, or companies that provide medical services or health-related technology.
Healthcare employees organization
Healthcare employees are people who work for hospitals, clinics, medical offices, or related health services.
healthcare organizations organization
Healthcare organizations are groups that provide, support, or manage healthcare services.
healthcare sector organization
The healthcare sector includes hospitals, clinics, insurers, and other organizations that provide or support medical care.
helpdesk organization
A helpdesk is a support team that helps users with account, computer, and access problems.
Hephaestus threat-actor
Hephaestus is a named threat actor, malware, tool, or campaign referenced in security reporting.
high severity concept
High severity means a security issue is considered serious and should usually be fixed quickly.
hijacking technique
Hijacking in cybersecurity means taking control of something, such as a browser session, account, or network setting, without permission.
historical DNS concept
Historical DNS is archived domain-name lookup data that shows which IP addresses a domain used in the past.
Home Office organization
The Home Office is the UK government department responsible for immigration, security, policing, and related matters.
hook technique
A hook is a way for software to intercept or alter another program's behavior, often by catching function calls or events.
Hooks concept
Hooks are points where software can run custom code when certain events happen.
hosted concept
Hosted means a service, website, or system is running on someone’s server so other people can access it.
hostname concept
A hostname is the human-readable name assigned to a computer or server on a network.
hostnames concept
Hostnames are human-readable names assigned to computers or services on a network.
HTML phishing page technique
An HTML phishing page is a fake web page built with HTML to trick people into entering passwords or other sensitive information.
HTTP protocol
HTTP is a common way for computers to send web requests and responses over a network.

HTTP Referer is a web request header that can tell a website which page a visitor came from.
also: Referer, referer domains
HTTP Request Smuggling technique
HTTP Request Smuggling is an attack that tricks web servers and proxies into disagreeing about where one request ends and another begins.
HTTP traffic protocol
HTTP traffic is the web data sent between a browser or app and a website using the basic Hypertext Transfer Protocol.
HTTPS protocol
HTTPS is the secure version of the web protocol used to protect data sent between your browser and a website.
hubspot
HubSpot is a cloud platform for marketing, sales, customer support, and customer relationship management.
Hugging Face organization
Hugging Face is a company and platform for sharing machine learning models, datasets, and AI tools.
also: AI platform
human in the loop concept
Human in the loop means a person reviews, approves, or guides an automated system’s decisions instead of leaving it fully autonomous.
human risk concept
Human risk is the chance that people’s actions, mistakes, or decisions will cause a security problem.
Human Risk Management concept
Human Risk Management focuses on reducing security risk caused by people’s behavior through training, controls, and measurement.
Human Risk Management Purchasing Toolkit product
Human Risk Management Purchasing Toolkit is a resource kit for helping organizations buy tools or services that reduce security risks caused by human behavior.
human trafficking concept
Human trafficking is the crime of exploiting people through force, fraud, or coercion for labor, services, or sex.
Human-in-the-loop interactions concept
Human-in-the-loop interactions are steps where a person actively reviews, approves, guides, or corrects what an automated system is doing.
huntress organization
Huntress is a cybersecurity company providing managed detection and response for small and midsize organizations.
hyperledger product
hyperledger is a named package, project, or account referenced in security reporting, using the name of the Hyperledger blockchain project ecosystem.
IaaS concept
A cloud service model providing virtualized computing resources over the internet, like storage and virtual machines.
iCloud product
Apple's cloud storage and computing service, used to sync data across devices, often targeted for account takeover via phishing.
identities concept
Identities are accounts or actors that systems recognize and allow to access resources.
identity attacks concept
Identity attacks are attempts to steal, misuse, or bypass someone’s login identity or account access.
iframe concept
An iframe is an HTML element that embeds one web page inside another web page.
IIS machine keys concept
IIS machine keys are cryptographic keys used by Microsoft web applications to protect data such as authentication tokens and view state.
impersonate technique
To impersonate means to pretend to be someone else, often to trick people or systems.
impersonation technique
Impersonation is pretending to be someone or something trusted in order to deceive people or systems.
impersonation scams technique
Impersonation scams are frauds where criminals pretend to be a trusted person, company, or authority to trick victims into sending money or information.
implant malware
An implant is malware secretly placed on a computer so an attacker can keep access, run commands, or steal information later.
in memory concept
In memory means something runs or exists in a computer’s temporary working memory rather than as a normal file on disk.
In vitro fertilization concept
In vitro fertilization is a medical fertility treatment where an egg is fertilized outside the body and then placed in the uterus.
in-the-wild exploitation concept
In-the-wild exploitation means attackers are using a flaw in real-world activity rather than only in testing or research.
inbound concept
Inbound traffic is network communication that comes into a device or organization from an outside source.
inbox concept
An inbox is where incoming messages, requests, or federated activity items are received.
Incident concept
A security incident is an event that may harm systems, data, or users and needs investigation or response.
incident response concept
Incident response is the process of investigating and handling a security problem after it is found.
incidents concept
Incidents are security events that may harm systems, data, users, or business operations and need investigation or response.
india
India is a South Asian country often referenced in cybersecurity stories involving technology, government, and large organizations.
indicator concept
An indicator is a clue such as an IP address, file hash, domain, or email that may point to malicious activity.
indicator of compromise concept
An indicator of compromise is a sign that can help show a system may have been targeted or affected.
indicators concept
Indicators are clues such as IP addresses, domains, file hashes, or behaviors that may point to malicious activity.
Indicators of Compromise concept
Indicators of Compromise are clues such as addresses, file names, or patterns that can show malicious activity happened.
also: IOCs
Indicators of Future Attack® concept
Indicators of Future Attack are signals that identify attacker infrastructure and patterns before exploitation begins.
also: IOFA, Indicators of Future Attack® data
indonesia
Indonesia is a Southeast Asian country that may be mentioned in cybersecurity reporting as a location, target, or government context.
infect concept
To infect a computer or website means to place harmful software on it.
Infected concept
Infected means a device or system has been compromised by malware or unauthorized code.
infection chain concept
An infection chain is the step-by-step path an attack follows to get malicious software onto a device and make it run.
information disclosure vulnerability
Information disclosure is a weakness where software reveals data that should have stayed private.
Information operations technique
Information operations are organized efforts to influence, disrupt, or manipulate what people or organizations know and believe.
infostealer malware
An infostealer is malware designed to secretly collect passwords, browser data, and other valuable information.
Infrastructure context concept
Infrastructure context is background information about the servers, domains, IP addresses, and services involved in an online activity.
infrastructure intelligence concept
Infrastructure intelligence is information about internet infrastructure such as domains, IP addresses, servers, and hosting used by organizations or attackers.
Infrastructure patterns concept
Infrastructure patterns are repeated clues in how servers, domains, IP addresses, and hosting services are set up or reused.
initial access vector technique
An initial access vector is the method an attacker first uses to get into a target environment.
Inline task references concept
Inline task references are task links or identifiers placed directly inside code, text, or configuration instead of being stored separately.
also: tasking references, references
install scripts technique
Install scripts are commands that run automatically when software is installed and can be useful or risky depending on what they do.
install time concept
Install time is the moment when software is being installed, which attackers may abuse to run unwanted code.
Integrations concept
Integrations are connections that let different apps or services work together and share data.
intelligence community organization
The intelligence community is the group of government agencies that collect and analyze information about threats, foreign governments, and national security issues.
Intent concept
Intent is the goal or purpose behind an action, such as what a user or attacker is trying to accomplish.
Interactive terminal renderer tool
An interactive terminal renderer is software that displays a live command-line interface and lets users type commands into it.
also: terminal renderer
Internal data concept
Internal data is information meant to stay within an organization, such as records, documents, or system details.
Internal network concept
An internal network is the private network used inside an organization, separate from the public internet.
Internal platform product
An internal platform is software or infrastructure used inside an organization by its own employees or systems.
internal systems concept
Internal systems are an organization’s private computers, applications, and networks used for business operations.
internet access concept
Internet access means the ability for a device, user, or system to connect to online services and websites.
Internet exposure concept
Internet exposure means a system or service can be reached from the public internet, which can make it easier to attack.
internet gateways product
Internet gateways are devices or services that connect a local network to the wider internet and help route traffic between them.
Internet Information Services product
Internet Information Services is Microsoft's web server software for hosting websites and web applications on Windows.
INTERPOL organization
INTERPOL is an international police organization that helps countries cooperate on cross-border crime, including cybercrime.
intrusion concept
An intrusion is an unauthorized entry into a computer system or network.
Intrusion window concept
An intrusion window is the period of time when attackers had access to a system or network.
Investigate tool
Investigate is a named feature, workflow step, or tool function used to examine security events or suspicious activity.
investigation concept
An investigation is the process of examining evidence to understand what happened.
Investigatory Powers Tribunal organization
The Investigatory Powers Tribunal is a UK body that handles complaints about surveillance and intelligence-agency powers.
investment fraud concept
Investment fraud is a scam that tricks people into putting money into fake or misleading investment opportunities.
IONOS organization
IONOS is a web hosting, domain registration, and cloud services provider.
iota product
iota is a named package, project, or account referenced in security reporting, and may refer to the IOTA distributed-ledger ecosystem depending on context.
IP addresses protocol
IP addresses are numerical internet addresses used to locate computers, servers, or other networked systems.
IP cameras product
IP cameras are security cameras that connect to a network or the internet using an IP address.

IPv4 protocol
IPv4 is the older and still widely used internet address system that gives devices numeric addresses such as 192.0.2.1.
ironscales organization
IRONSCALES is an email security company focused on phishing detection and response.
Irregular organization
Irregular is an organization referenced in technology and security reporting, often associated with AI safety and security research.
issue-analyze.yml workflow tool
issue-analyze.yml workflow is a GitHub Actions workflow file that likely automates analysis of GitHub issues.
jailbreaks technique
Jailbreaks are attempts to make an AI system bypass its normal restrictions or safeguards.
Jaredwray other
Jaredwray is a named person or maintainer account referenced in software or security reporting.
JavaScript concept
JavaScript is a programming language commonly used to build software and web applications.

JavaScript injection is an attack where unwanted JavaScript code is inserted into a web page or app so it runs in a user's browser.

johnnysilverhe threat-actor
johnnysilverhe is an online account or handle referenced in security reporting.
also: threat actor named "johnnysilverhe"
journalists other

Kaspersky organization
Kaspersky is a cybersecurity company known for antivirus and other security products.

Kerberos is a network authentication protocol that lets users and services prove their identity securely using tickets.
keylogging

Keystroke logging technique
Keystroke logging is secretly recording what someone types, often to steal passwords, messages, or other sensitive information.

keyv@6.0.0 tool

Kion is a brand or organization name referenced in technology and security reporting, often needing context to identify precisely.

A U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency list of vulnerabilities that are actively being exploited in the wild.

Known vulnerability databases are public or private lists of documented security flaws that defenders use to find and prioritize fixes.
Kod.ru organization
Kod.ru is a Russian technology media or online publication name referenced in reporting.
Krzysztof Gawkowski organization
Krzysztof Gawkowski is a Polish politician associated with digital affairs and government technology policy.
Kubernetes product

Large language models are AI systems trained on huge amounts of text so they can generate and understand human-like language.
lateral movement technique

law enforcement organization
Law enforcement means police or government agencies responsible for investigating and stopping crime.
law enforcement agencies organization
Law enforcement agencies are organizations responsible for enforcing laws and investigating crime.
Law enforcement impersonation technique
Law enforcement impersonation is when a scammer pretends to be police or another official authority to pressure a victim into obeying.
Law enforcement impersonation scams technique
Law enforcement impersonation scams are fraud schemes where criminals pretend to be police or government investigators to scare victims into paying money or sharing information.
Legal notices concept
Legal notices are formal messages that state legal rights, warnings, obligations, or claims.
Legion Loader malware

Legitimate cloud services concept
Legitimate cloud services are real online platforms that attackers may abuse to host files, send messages, or hide activity.
lego-education product
lego-education is a named package, project, or account referenced in security reporting, likely using a name associated with LEGO Education.
Liberty organization
Liberty is a named organization, product, or project referenced in security reporting.
Licenses concept
Licenses are legal rules that say how software, data, or content may be used, copied, or shared.
also: license
Line mode concept
Line mode is an input mode where a program waits for a complete line of text before processing it.
Lineage concept
Lineage is the history of where a file, package, model, or artifact came from and how it changed over time.
LitRes organization
LitRes is a Russian digital book and audiobook service.
Living Security organization
Living Security is a cybersecurity company focused on security awareness and human risk management.

loader-as-a-service concept
Loader-as-a-service is a criminal business model where operators rent malware that installs other malware for customers.
also: LaaS, loader service, service
localhost concept
Localhost is the name a computer uses to refer to itself on a network.

Lockfiles record the exact versions of software dependencies a project uses so builds are more predictable.
login credentials concept
Information like usernames and passwords used to access accounts.
login page concept
A login page is the screen or web page where a user enters credentials such as a username and password to access an account.
lookalike-domains

lure technique
A lure is bait used by attackers, such as a fake offer or message, to persuade someone to click or act.
lures technique
Lures are messages, files, or themes attackers use to tempt people into clicking a link, opening an attachment, or taking another risky action.
machine keys concept
Machine keys are cryptographic settings used by web applications to protect data such as authentication tokens and view state.

Machine-key extraction is stealing a server’s secret machine key so attackers can forge or decrypt protected application data.
macOS product
macOS is Apple’s operating system for Mac computers.
macOS product
Apple's desktop operating system for Mac computers.
macOS malware malware
macOS malware is harmful software designed to infect or abuse Apple Mac computers.
mail server tool
A mail server is a computer system that sends, receives, and stores email for users or organizations.
main branch concept
The main branch is the primary line of development in a source-code repository where the current version of a project is usually kept.
maintainer credentials concept
Maintainer credentials are passwords, tokens, or keys used by software project maintainers to manage and publish code.
Maintainers concept
Maintainers are the people responsible for updating, reviewing, and managing a software project.
Malicious concept
Malicious means intentionally harmful, such as software or behavior designed to damage, steal, or deceive.
malicious activity concept
Malicious activity is any harmful or unauthorized action, such as stealing data, spreading malware, or breaking into systems.
malicious code concept
Malicious code is software instructions written to harm systems, steal data, or give attackers control.
Malicious content concept
Malicious content is any file, link, code, or message designed to harm users or systems.
malicious JavaScript malware
Malicious JavaScript is harmful code written in the JavaScript language that runs in browsers or websites to steal data, redirect users, or perform unwanted actions.
malicious link concept
A malicious link is a web link designed to lead someone to malware, scams, fake login pages, or other harmful content.
Malicious links technique
Malicious links are web links designed to trick users into visiting harmful pages, downloading malware, or giving away information.
malicious package malware
A malicious package is a software package that contains harmful code or was created to trick users into installing it.
malicious packages malware
Malicious packages are software libraries published or shared with harmful code hidden inside them.
malicious pull request technique
A malicious pull request is a proposed code change that secretly tries to add harmful code or weaken a project's security.
malicious software concept
Malicious software is software designed to harm systems, steal information, or give attackers control.
malicious URL concept
A malicious URL is a web link designed to lead people to malware, phishing pages, or other harmful content.
malware concept
Malware is software made to harm, spy on, or take control of computers or data.
malware campaign concept
A malware campaign is a coordinated effort to spread malicious software to many targets.
malware delivery technique
Malware delivery is the process attackers use to get malicious software onto a victim's device.
malware families concept
Malware families are groups of related malicious programs that share code, behavior, or a common creator.
Managed endpoints concept
Managed endpoints are user devices or servers that an IT or security team centrally monitors, updates, and controls.
mangorbit[.]com other
mangorbit[.]com is a defanged domain name referenced in security reporting, likely as part of suspicious or malicious infrastructure.

Manifold Security is a cybersecurity company or research organization name referenced in security reporting.

MariaDB is an open-source relational database system created as a community-developed alternative to MySQL.
Markdown product
A lightweight text formatting syntax that's popular for documentation, also used in phishing kits and malware notes.
Mass surveillance concept
Mass surveillance is large-scale monitoring of people's communications, movements, or online activity.
Massive organization
Massive is a named entity referenced in security reporting, likely a tool, service, or organization name.
math_init.js tool
math_init.js is a JavaScript file name referenced in security reporting, potentially used as part of legitimate or malicious code.
Math_Symbol.js tool
Math_Symbol.js is a JavaScript file name referenced in security reporting, potentially used as part of legitimate or malicious code.
maven
Maven is a popular Java build and dependency management tool used to compile projects and download libraries.
MCP Server tool
An MCP Server is a server that implements the Model Context Protocol to connect AI systems with tools, data, or services.
also: MCP Server integration
MD5 protocol
MD5 is an older hashing method that creates a short fingerprint of data, but it is no longer considered secure for protecting information.
Measurable risk reduction concept
Measurable risk reduction means lowering security risk in a way that can be shown with numbers, evidence, or clear outcomes.
medical device manufacturers organization

Metadata is data that describes other data, such as when a file was created, who sent an email, or where a photo was taken.
metamask product

A microphone is a device that captures sound, which malware may try to access for spying.
microsoft organization

Microsoft sign-in page product

Microsoft Visual Studio Code product
Microsoft Visual Studio Code is a popular code editor used by developers to write and manage software.
microsoft-365

microsoft-exchange

microsoft-graph product

Military intelligence concept
Military intelligence is the collection and analysis of information to support a country’s armed forces and national security decisions.
Minecraft product

Mini Shai-Hulud appears to be a smaller variant or related name of the Shai-Hulud malware.
Ministry of Defence organization
A Ministry of Defence is a government department responsible for a country's military and national defense policy.

Misconfiguration is an unsafe or incorrect setting that can expose a system to attack.
misuse concept
Misuse is using a system, account, or feature in a harmful or unauthorized way.

Mitigation strategies are steps taken to reduce the likelihood or impact of a security risk or attack.
mitigations concept
Mitigations are steps taken to reduce the chance or impact of a security problem.

MITRE ATT&CK is a public knowledge base that organizes common attacker tactics and techniques so defenders can describe and compare threats consistently.
mobile applications product

moxy tool

Mythos 5 product

n-central-take-control appears to refer to a Take Control remote-access component or related item associated with N-able N-central.

Netskope One platform is Netskope’s cloud security platform for protecting users, data, and applications across networks and cloud services.
Netskope Threat Labs organization
Netskope Threat Labs is the research team at Netskope that analyzes cyber threats and publishes security findings.
NetSuite product
A cloud-based business management suite for ERP and finance, a common target for phishing and credential theft.
network devices product
Network devices are hardware such as routers, switches, firewalls, and access points that move or protect network traffic.
network traffic concept
Network traffic is the data moving between computers, servers, phones, and other devices over a network.
neutral concept
A state or position that does not take sides in a conflict, or remains impartial in a security or political context.
NGSWG organization
NGSWG is an acronym for a named working group referenced in security or policy reporting.
Niebezpiecznik organization
Niebezpiecznik is a Polish cybersecurity news and education website.
NIST organization
NIST is the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology, which creates widely used security standards and guidance.
NLAW tool
NLAW is a named tool or project referenced in security reporting.
Node product
Node usually refers to Node.js, a runtime that lets JavaScript run outside a web browser.
non-automatable concept
Non-automatable means a task cannot realistically be completed by software alone and needs human judgment or action.
non-human identity concept
Digital credentials used by machines, services, applications, or APIs instead of human users.
NordVPN product
NordVPN is a commercial virtual private network service used to route internet traffic through encrypted VPN servers.
north-korea other
North Korea is a country often referenced in cybersecurity reports because some hacking groups are alleged to operate on its behalf.
Notification numbers concept
Notification numbers are reference numbers used to track official notices, alerts, or reports.
npm product
npm is the main package manager and public registry for JavaScript software libraries.
also: npm registry, npm package pages
npm install tool
npm install is the command developers use to download and set up JavaScript packages from the npm ecosystem.
npm package concept
An npm package is a reusable JavaScript software bundle that developers can install from the npm ecosystem.
npm packages product
npm packages are reusable JavaScript software modules distributed through the npm package ecosystem.
npm tokens concept
npm tokens are secret access keys used to authenticate to the npm package registry.
npm update tool
npm update is a command that updates JavaScript packages installed through the npm package manager.
npm-cache[.]com other
npm-cache[.]com is a suspicious domain name that appears to imitate the npm software package ecosystem.
npm-lifecycle-scripts
NPM lifecycle scripts are commands that run automatically during package install or build steps and can be abused to execute malicious code.
npm-preinstall technique
npm-preinstall refers to the npm package-install stage where a script can run before installation finishes, which can be misused for malware execution.
npm-preinstall-script technique
npm-preinstall-script is a term referring to code that runs automatically before an npm package is installed, which attackers can abuse to execute malicious commands.
nuget
NuGet is Microsoft’s package manager for .NET software libraries.
OAuth protocol
An authorization protocol that allows a user to grant a third-party application limited access to their resources without sharing their password.
OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant protocol
OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant is a login flow that lets devices with limited input, like TVs, sign in through another device such as a phone or computer.
OAuth code phishing technique
OAuth code phishing is a trick where attackers steal an authorization code from a login flow so they can gain access to an account or app.
also: OAuth code phishing operations
OAuth consent abuse technique
OAuth consent abuse is when attackers trick users into approving a malicious app so it can access their accounts without stealing their password.
OAuth tokens protocol
OAuth tokens are digital access passes that let one service connect to another without sharing a password each time.
obfuscated technique
Obfuscated means code or text has been deliberately made hard to read so people or security tools cannot easily understand what it does.
Obfuscated JavaScript stealer malware
An obfuscated JavaScript stealer is malicious JavaScript code that is deliberately made hard to read and is designed to steal data from a victim.
Odoo product
Odoo is a business software platform that provides apps for functions like sales, accounting, inventory, and websites.
offensive cyber concept
Offensive cyber refers to cyber operations intended to disrupt, spy on, or gain access to an adversary's systems.
offensive security concept
Offensive security is the practice of testing systems by thinking and acting like an attacker to find weaknesses before criminals do.
OIDC protocol
OIDC stands for OpenID Connect, a protocol that helps apps confirm a user's identity during sign-in.
OIDC tokens protocol
OIDC tokens are digital proof that a user or service has authenticated through OpenID Connect.
OIDC trusted publishing technique
OIDC trusted publishing lets a software build system prove its identity with OpenID Connect so it can publish packages without storing a long-lived password or token.
Omada product
Omada is TP-Link's business networking product line for managing devices such as access points, switches, and gateways.
also: Omada network devices, Omada Controllers, Omada Controller, Omada deployment
on-premises concept
On-premises means software or hardware runs in an organization’s own facilities instead of in the cloud.
on-premises SharePoint servers product
On-premises SharePoint servers are Microsoft SharePoint systems hosted and managed inside an organization rather than in Microsoft’s cloud.
Onboarding concept
Onboarding is the process of setting up a new user, employee, device, or service so it can start working safely.
OneDrive product
OneDrive is Microsoft's cloud storage service for saving and syncing files online.
onereach product
onereach is a named package, project, or account referenced in security reporting.
online fraud concept
Online fraud is using the internet to trick people or organizations out of money, goods, or information.
Online Safety concept
Online Safety refers to policies and practices intended to reduce harm, abuse, fraud, and other risks on the internet.
open internet access concept
Open internet access means a system or user can connect broadly to websites and online services without tight restrictions.
open source concept
Open source means software whose source code is publicly available for people to inspect, use, modify, and share.
open source packages product
Open source packages are reusable pieces of software code that anyone can inspect and often include in their own projects.
Open VSX marketplace product
Open VSX marketplace is an open registry where developers publish and download extensions for VS Code-compatible editors.
open-source dependencies concept
Open-source dependencies are publicly available software components that a project relies on to work.
open-source project concept
An open-source project is software whose source code is publicly available for people to inspect, use, modify, or contribute to.
Open-source supply chain concept
The open-source supply chain is the chain of public software libraries, maintainers, and repositories that applications depend on.
open-vsx
Open VSX is an open-source marketplace for Visual Studio Code-compatible extensions.
openai organization
OpenAI is an AI company known for ChatGPT and GPT language models.
OpenAI models product
OpenAI models are artificial intelligence systems made by OpenAI that can understand or generate text, code, images, or other content.
OpenClaw product
OpenClaw is a named tool or project, but I cannot define it confidently from the term alone.
OpenID Connect protocol
OpenID Connect is an identity layer on top of OAuth 2.0 that lets apps verify who a user is.
Opera product
Opera is a web browser based on Chromium with built-in features such as ad blocking and VPN-like browsing options.
Operating system concept
An operating system is the main software that manages a computer or phone, such as Windows, macOS, Android, or iOS.
operating-system-level compromise concept
Operating-system-level compromise means an attacker has gained control deep enough to affect the core software running a device.
Operation chat concept
Operation chat is a communication channel or feature used to coordinate activity during an operation or investigation.
also: chat interface, general chat
Operational workflows concept
Operational workflows are the step-by-step processes teams use to get routine work done.
Operator tool
An Operator is a Kubernetes automation component that manages an application by encoding operational tasks into software.
Operator aliases concept
Operator aliases are nicknames or handles used by attackers, scammers, or security operators instead of their real names.
also: alias
operator panel tool
An operator panel is a control interface used by administrators or attackers to manage a system, tool, or campaign.
operators concept
Operators are the people or groups running a system, service, campaign, or criminal operation.
or-sdk tool
or-sdk is a named software development kit or package referenced in security reporting.
OR-Tools tool
Google's open-source software suite for mathematical optimization and operations research problems.
Oracle VM VirtualBox product
Oracle VM VirtualBox is virtualization software that lets a computer run other operating systems inside virtual machines.
also: vboxservice.exe
Organizational context concept
Organizational context is background information about a company or agency that helps explain its risks, systems, and decisions.
Ornikar organization
Ornikar is a French online driving school and car insurance services company.
Out-of-bounds vulnerability
Out-of-bounds means software reads or writes outside the memory area it was supposed to use, which can cause crashes or security bugs.
Out-of-policy behavior concept
Out-of-policy behavior means actions that break an organization's stated rules or security requirements.
outbound concept
Outbound traffic is network communication that leaves a device or organization and goes to an outside destination.
Outlook product
Outlook is Microsoft's email and calendar application used by individuals and organizations.
Ozon organization
Ozon is a major Russian e-commerce marketplace and online retail company.
PaaS concept
A cloud computing model where a provider offers a platform allowing customers to develop, run, and manage applications without maintaining infrastructure.
package metadata concept
Package metadata is the basic information about a software package, such as its name, version, author, and dependencies.
package versions concept
Package versions are numbered releases of software components that help track updates and fixes.
package.json concept
package.json is a file used in Node.js projects to list project details, dependencies, scripts, and settings.
Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 organization
Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 is a threat intelligence and incident response team within Palo Alto Networks.
Palo Alto Unit 42 organization
Palo Alto Unit 42 is the threat-intelligence and incident-response research team at Palo Alto Networks.
also: Unit42
particularly sensitive personal data concept
Particularly sensitive personal data is information such as health, financial, biometric, or private identity data that can cause serious harm if exposed.
Patch Tuesday concept
Patch Tuesday is Microsoft's regular monthly release day for security updates, usually the second Tuesday of each month.
patched concept
Patched means a software flaw has been fixed with an update.
patches concept
Patches are software updates that fix bugs, security flaws, or other problems.
patching concept
Applying software updates to fix security holes and bugs.
pavel-durov
Pavel Durov is the founder and CEO of Telegram.
Pay-as-you-go pricing concept
Pay-as-you-go pricing means paying only for the services or resources you actually use instead of paying a fixed upfront amount.
Pay-or-leak technique
Pay-or-leak is an extortion tactic where criminals demand money and threaten to publish stolen data if the victim refuses.
Pay-or-leak data extortion model technique
The pay-or-leak data extortion model is when criminals steal data and demand payment by threatening to publish it.
payload concept
A payload is the part of malicious code that performs the attacker’s intended action.
Payload Builder Pane tool
A Payload Builder Pane is a software interface area used to configure or generate code or files that will be delivered as a payload.
Payload type container concept
A payload type container is a software container that packages the code and settings needed to build or run a particular kind of Mythic payload.
payloads concept
Payloads are the parts of malware or an exploit that perform the attacker's intended action, such as stealing data or installing ransomware.
Payment details concept
Payment details are information used to pay for something, such as card numbers, billing addresses, or bank account data.
Payment fraud concept
Payment fraud is the unauthorized or deceptive use of payment methods to steal money or goods.
payment information concept
Payment information is data used to make purchases, such as card numbers, billing details, or payment account identifiers.
Payment systems concept
Payment systems are the services and networks that let people and businesses send, receive, and process money.
Penetration testing technique
Penetration testing is an authorized security test where people try to break into systems to find weaknesses before real attackers do.
Penetration Testing as a Service concept
Penetration Testing as a Service is a subscription-style service where experts continuously or regularly test systems for security weaknesses.
pentesting concept
Pentesting is authorized hacking performed to find and help fix security weaknesses.
permission boundaries concept
Permission boundaries are limits that cap what an identity can do, even if other policies grant broader access.
Permission model concept
A permission model defines who or what is allowed to access resources and perform actions in a system.
persistence concept
Persistence is the ability for an attacker to keep access to a system over time.
Persistence mechanisms technique
Persistence mechanisms are ways attackers keep access to a system even after restarts, password changes, or cleanup attempts.
persistent access concept
Persistent access means continued access to an account or system over time.
Persistent remote access technique
Persistent remote access means an attacker keeps a way to reconnect to a system even after reboots or temporary disruptions.
personal access token concept
A personal access token is a secret code used instead of a password to let apps or scripts access an online account or service.
personal data concept
Information relating to an identifiable individual, such as name, email, location, or financial details.
personally identifiable information concept
Personally identifiable information is data that can identify a person, such as a name, address, Social Security number, or email address.
Phish concept
Phish is a label for a deceptive message designed to trick a recipient.
phishing technique
Phishing is a scam where attackers impersonate trusted people or services to steal information or make victims take unsafe actions.
phishing attacks technique
Deceptive emails or messages that trick recipients into revealing personal information or installing malware.
phishing campaign technique
A phishing campaign is a coordinated effort to trick people into giving up passwords, money, or other sensitive information.
phishing campaigns technique
Phishing campaigns are organized attempts to trick many people into revealing information or installing malware using fake messages.
phishing email technique
A phishing email is a fake or deceptive message designed to trick someone into revealing information or clicking something harmful.
phishing emails technique
Phishing emails are fake messages designed to trick people into revealing information or clicking harmful links.
phishing infrastructure concept
Phishing infrastructure is the set of websites, servers, domains, and tools criminals use to run phishing scams.
Phishing lure technique
A phishing lure is the fake message, link, or story used to trick someone into clicking or sharing information.
Phishing page technique
A phishing page is a fake web page designed to trick people into entering passwords, payment details, or other sensitive information.
phishing pages technique
Phishing pages are fake web pages designed to trick people into entering passwords, codes, or other sensitive information.
phishing-as-a-service concept
Phishing-as-a-service is a criminal service that sells ready-made tools and infrastructure for running phishing attacks.
phishing-for-information technique
Phishing for information is when attackers trick people into revealing sensitive details such as passwords, codes, or personal data.
Phishing-resistant authentication concept
Phishing-resistant authentication is a login method designed so fake websites cannot easily steal or reuse the user’s credentials.
also: passkeys
phishing-resistant MFA concept
Phishing-resistant MFA is multi-factor authentication designed so fake login pages cannot easily steal or reuse the login proof.
phone calls protocol
Phone calls are voice conversations made over telephone networks or internet calling services.
Picsart organization
Picsart is a photo and video editing app and online creative platform.
Pillar Security organization
Pillar Security is a cybersecurity company or organization referenced in security reporting.
PIN concept
A PIN is a short numeric code used to unlock a device, card, or account.
pinned concept
Pinned means fixed to a specific version, commit, certificate, or value so it does not change unexpectedly.
Pipeline concept
A pipeline is an automated sequence of steps used to build, test, or deploy software.
pivot technique
A pivot is an investigative move where one clue is used to find another related clue, such as moving from a domain to linked IP addresses.
pivoting technique
Pivoting is when an attacker uses one compromised system as a stepping stone to reach other systems or networks.
PNG concept
PNG is a common image file format used for pictures, logos, and screenshots.
also: steganographic PNG image, malware-laced PNG images
PNG images concept
PNG images are a common picture file format that attackers may sometimes use to hide or deliver data.
poland other
Poland is a country in Europe.
Poland's data protection authority organization
Poland's data protection authority is the national regulator that enforces privacy and personal-data protection laws in Poland.
Poland's Minister of Digital Affairs organization
Poland's Minister of Digital Affairs is the government official responsible for Poland's digital policy and technology-related public services.
Polish Data Protection Authority organization
The Polish Data Protection Authority is Poland's government regulator responsible for enforcing privacy and data protection rules.
Polish Ministry of Digital Affairs organization
The Polish Ministry of Digital Affairs is a Polish government organization responsible for national digital policy and related services.
Polygon product
Polygon is a blockchain network designed to make Ethereum-compatible transactions faster and cheaper.
Poseidon malware
Poseidon is a named tool, malware family, or project referenced in security reporting.
Post-compromise activity technique
Post-compromise activity is what attackers do after they have already broken into a system.
Powercat tool
Powercat is a PowerShell-based networking tool similar to netcat that can be used for testing or abused by attackers for remote connections.
powershell
PowerShell is Microsoft’s command-line shell and scripting language, often used by administrators and abused by attackers.
also: PowerShell command
PowerShell commands tool
PowerShell commands are instructions run in Microsoft's powerful Windows automation shell, often used by administrators and attackers alike.
pr-analyze.yml tool
pr-analyze.yml is a workflow configuration file likely used to automatically analyze pull requests in a software project.
preinstall technique
preinstall is a package script that runs automatically before software is installed, often in npm packages.
preinstall hook technique
A preinstall hook is a script that runs automatically before a software package is installed, which attackers can abuse to run malicious code.
preinstall script technique
A preinstall script is code that runs automatically before a software package is installed, which can be useful but risky if abused.
also: preinstall command
Premium-SMS subscription concept
A premium-SMS subscription is a paid text-message service that charges a user's phone bill, sometimes abused by scams.
also: premium-rate SMS service, SMS deep link
Preparation concept
Preparation is the incident-response phase where teams plan, train, and set up tools before an attack happens.
preparedness concept
The state of being ready to handle or respond to a security incident, including plans, training, and tools.
Primary care networks organization
Primary care networks are groups of local healthcare providers that coordinate basic medical services for patients.
Primary Refresh Token protocol
A Primary Refresh Token is a Microsoft identity token that helps keep a user signed in to cloud-connected Windows services.
Prioritization concept
Prioritization means deciding which issues or tasks should be handled first based on importance or risk.
Privacy International organization
Privacy International is a nonprofit organization that advocates for privacy rights and challenges intrusive surveillance practices.
private data concept
Sensitive information that should not be publicly disclosed, like personal identifiers or financial records.
private key concept
A private key is secret cryptographic data used to prove identity or decrypt information and must be kept confidential.
private keys concept
Private keys are secret cryptographic values used to prove identity, decrypt data, or authorize cryptocurrency transactions.
private repository concept
A private repository is a restricted code storage location that only approved users can access.
privilege-escalation technique
Privilege escalation is when an attacker gains higher levels of access than they were supposed to have.
privileged code-fixing agent tool
A privileged code-fixing agent is an automated tool with elevated access that can change code to repair issues, making it powerful and risky if misused.
privileges concept
Privileges are permissions that determine what actions a user or process is allowed to perform on a system.
process memory concept
Process memory is the part of a computer’s memory used by a running program.
Process Monitor tool
Process Monitor is a Microsoft Sysinternals tool that records file, registry, process, and network activity on Windows.
also: procmon.exe
production database concept
A production database is the live database used by a real application or service, often containing actual user or business data.
Prompt concept
A prompt is the instruction or question a person gives to an AI system to guide its response.
prompt engineering technique
Prompt engineering is the practice of carefully wording instructions to get better or safer answers from an AI system.
prompt injection technique
Prompt injection is a way of giving an AI system instructions that may make it behave in unintended ways.
prompt-injected technique
Prompt-injected means an AI system has been manipulated by hidden or malicious instructions placed in the text it reads.
prompt-injection instructions technique
Prompt-injection instructions are hidden or malicious text commands meant to trick an AI system into ignoring its rules or doing something unsafe.
prompts concept
Prompts are the instructions or questions a user gives to an AI system to get a response.
proof-of-concept technique
A working demonstration, often a piece of code, that proves a security vulnerability can actually be exploited.
prototype code concept
Prototype code is early test code built to prove an idea before it is made reliable, secure, or production-ready.
Provenance concept
Provenance means the origin and history of something, such as where software came from and how it was built.
also: attestation
Provider working groups organization
Provider working groups are collaborative groups of service providers that coordinate on shared policy, technical, or security issues.
proxy concept
A proxy is an intermediate server that forwards internet traffic between a user and a destination.
proxy services concept
Proxy services route internet traffic through another server, often to filter, hide, monitor, or redirect connections.
Public GitHub repository product
A public GitHub repository is a code project on GitHub that anyone on the internet can view.
also: shared GitHub repository
Public internet concept
The public internet is the globally accessible network that anyone can connect to through internet service providers.
also: live internet
public IP address concept
A public IP address is an internet-reachable network address that can be accessed from outside a private network.
also: victim's public IP address, victim machine's public IPv4 address

Public registries are open online repositories where people publish and download software packages, container images, or other shared components.
pull request concept
A pull request is a request to review and merge code changes into a shared software project.
pull requests concept
Pull requests are proposals to merge code changes into a software project, commonly used on platforms like GitHub.
pypi
PyPI is the main public package repository for Python software libraries.
Python tool
Python is a popular programming language often used to write scripts, automation tools, and security research code.
qBittorrent tool
qBittorrent is a free BitTorrent file-sharing application used to download and share files over peer-to-peer networks.
Qlik organization
Qlik is a software company known for business intelligence, analytics, and data integration products.
QR concept
QR usually refers to a QR code, a square barcode that phones can scan to open links or store information.
also: QR code
quarantine technique
Quarantine is a holding area where suspicious files or emails are isolated so they cannot cause harm right away.
RabbitMQ tool
RabbitMQ is message-broker software that lets different parts of an application send messages to each other reliably.
also: RabbitMQ-based RPC system
race condition vulnerability
A race condition is a bug where software behaves unpredictably because two operations happen in an unexpected order or at the same time.
ransom demand concept
A ransom demand is a message from criminals asking for payment, usually to unlock systems or stop leaked data from being published.
Ransomware gang threat-actor
A ransomware gang is a criminal group that uses malware or data theft to demand payment from victims.

A RAT, or remote access trojan, is malware that lets an attacker remotely control an infected device.
Raw key mode technique
Raw key mode is an input mode where a program receives each keypress directly instead of waiting for a full line of text.
React2Shell vulnerability
React2Shell is a named vulnerability or exploit label associated with React-related security reporting.
Real time concept
Real time means something happens or is shown immediately, or with very little delay.
Reasoning concept
Reasoning is the process of working through information logically to reach an answer or decision.
redirect concept

reflection technique

Registry concept
The Registry is a Windows database that stores system and application settings.

registry.npmjs[.]org/-/whoami is an npm registry API endpoint used to check which npm account a token belongs to.
regulator concept
A regulator is an organization that oversees and enforces rules in a specific area.
relay concept

Relay servers concept
Relay servers pass network traffic or messages between other systems, often to help connections reach their destination.
also: relay server
reliaquest organization
ReliaQuest is a cybersecurity company offering managed detection, response, and security operations tools.
remediation technique
Remediation is the work of fixing a security problem and reducing the damage it caused.
remote access trojan malware
A remote access trojan is malware that secretly lets an attacker control a victim's computer from somewhere else.
remote attacker concept
A remote attacker is someone who tries to exploit a system over a network without needing physical access to it.
remote attackers concept
Remote attackers are people who try to affect a system over a network rather than by physically accessing it.
remote control technique
Remote control means operating a computer, phone, or system from another location over a network.
remote management tools tool

Remote monitoring and management tool
Remote monitoring and management is software that lets IT staff watch and control computers or networks from afar.

Remote Support product
Remote Support is software or a service that lets a technician connect to a user’s device from another location to help fix problems.
remote-code-execution technique

also: RCE
Remotely tool
Remotely is a remote administration tool that can be used to access and manage computers over a network.
Renderer concept
A renderer is the part of a browser or app that turns code and content into what the user sees on screen.
repositories concept
Repositories are places where software project files and related development data are stored.
repository concept
A repository is a storage location for code, files, and their change history, especially in systems like GitHub.
request smuggling technique

researchers organization
Researchers are people who study systems, threats, or vulnerabilities to understand and improve security.
resilience concept
The ability of an organization to anticipate, withstand, and recover from adverse cyber events and security breaches.
Respond technique
Respond means to take action after detecting a security issue, such as containing an attack or fixing affected systems.
Restart concept

Reston other
Reston is a place name, most commonly referring to the town in Virginia that may appear in registration, hosting, or company-location details.
Resumable file transfers concept
Resumable file transfers let an interrupted upload or download continue from where it stopped instead of starting over.
also: resume, resuming
Retail operations concept
Retail operations are the day-to-day activities involved in running stores or selling goods to customers.
revocation concept
The process of invalidating a digital credential or certificate so it can no longer be used.

RFP, short for Request for Proposal, is a document an organization sends to vendors asking them to propose how they would meet a need and at what cost.
RingCentral organization
RingCentral is a cloud communications company that provides business phone, messaging, video, and contact-center services.

Risk Explorer is a named security product feature or tool used to explore and understand risks in an environment.
RMM tool
Software tools used by IT teams to manage computers remotely, sometimes abused by attackers to maintain persistent control over infected machines.
Roblox product
Roblox is an online gaming platform where users create and play games and buy virtual items.

romance concept

romance scams technique
Online fraud where criminals build fake romantic relationships to trick victims into sending money or sensitive information.
root privileges concept

rubygems

run code concept
To run code means to make a computer execute instructions written in a programming language.
runner tool

runOn: 'folderOpen' technique
runOn: 'folderOpen' is a Visual Studio Code extension setting that can make code run automatically when a folder is opened.
runtime concept

russia
Russia is a country frequently referenced in cybersecurity stories involving cybercrime groups, espionage, and government activity.
Russian forces organization
Russian forces are Russia's military units and personnel.
SaaS concept

SaaS platforms are online software services that users access through the internet rather than installing locally.
sabotage technique

SafeDep organization
SafeDep appears to be a security company or product focused on software supply chain risks.
safeguards concept
Safeguards are protections put in place to reduce the chance or impact of harm, misuse, or security incidents.
SAFER product
SAFER is a U.S. motor-carrier information system run by the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration.
salesforce product

sample data concept

A sandbox is an isolated environment used to run code more safely so it cannot easily affect the rest of the system.

sandboxes tool

Saved passwords concept
Saved passwords are login credentials stored by a browser, app, or password manager for later use.
